review_notes:
I read the whole file. Nearly all declarations are one-line wrappers around Order/Filter/Extr.lean, and those don't count under the rubric. The only repeated non-wrapper proof is the pair isLocalMax_of_mono_anti' and isLocalMin_of_anti_mono'. Their bodies are character-for-character identical. I did not run Lean, so I can't say the rewrite compiles. The sibling file's identical dual trick makes me expect it to. The evidence is at lines 561-577 here and at OrderClosedExtr.lean lines 32-46.

Two things in the candidate's wording are slightly off. The sketch says "a ∩ c-style membership", but the proof uses nhds_of_Ici_Iic to get a ∪ c ∈ 𝓝 b. The shared lemma is also not a new lemma. It is isLocalMax_of_mono_anti' itself, used at βᵒᵈ.

claims.reason: Lines 566-568 and 575-577 are the same proof. Each shows b ∈ a and b ∈ c with mem_of_mem_nhdsWithin, takes the neighbourhood from nhds_of_Ici_Iic ha hc, and closes with `rcases le_total x b <;> aesop`. The two statements are order duals. The hypotheses match exactly (same α, same ha and hc, Preorder β in both), so nothing is lost in the dualisation. The sibling file OrderClosedExtr.lean already does exactly this: `isLocalMin_of_anti_mono` is `isLocalMax_of_mono_anti (β := βᵒᵈ) g₀ g₁ h₀ h₁`, where AntitoneOn and IsLocalMin on β unfold to MonotoneOn and IsLocalMax on βᵒᵈ. Dependencies are acyclic, since the Min lemma comes after the Max lemma in the same file. The same file already uses this style in IsLocalMaxOn.not_nhds_le_map. The benefit is modest: the case-split argument, including its aesop call, is kept in one place instead of two. The reasoning is short, so this is a borderline but real instance of repeated machinery rather than routine unfolding.
